description: Hi, I’m Hiba from Team Astro1, solving the astronaut health monitoring challenge. During deep-space missions, forty-minute comms delays mean crew can’t wait for ground surgeons. Meet Offline Astro-Twin — an air-gapped health monitor grounded in CSA Radi-N2 and NASA Human Research Program data.
summary: Offline Astro-Twin is an air-gapped astronaut health monitoring system and local Flight Surgeon Copilot built for long-duration ISS, Lunar, and Mars missions where communication delays or solar blackouts cut off real-time ground support. Grounded in Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Radi-N2 radiation measurements and NASA Human Research Program (HRP) bone-loss benchmarks, it empowers non-physician crew members to detect physiological risks early through an interactive biometric body twin, plain-English self-exam protocols, actionable countermeasure simulations, and cited offline medical guidance.
details:
Long-duration spaceflight exposes astronauts to space radiation, microgravity bone/muscle unloading, isolation, and closed-loop cabin hazards—leading to Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), bone mineral density (BMD) loss, cardiovascular deconditioning, and behavioral fatigue. When missions push to the Moon (~2.6s round-trip) or Mars (up to ~44-minute round-trip light-time delay), astronauts carry primary responsibility for monitoring and acting on their own health.

Offline Astro-Twin delivers a complete, zero-internet onboard health workstation:

Interactive Biometric Body Twin: Visualizes Cardiovascular, Skeletal/Bone, Brain/Eyes (SANS & Behavioral), and Immune/Radiation systems with color-blind-safe status indicators (Green, Amber, Red, No Data) and strict per-metric data provenance chips (Real, Extrapolated, Synthetic, or Unverified Manual Entry).

Actionable Countermeasure & Self-Exam Guidance: Replaces passive disclaimers with plain-English self-exam instructions (e.g., Amsler visual grid, dosimeter checks), concrete NASA-documented preventive actions ("What You Can Do Now"), escalation triggers, and a "5 Core Questions" quick reference per body system.

7-Day Countermeasure Trajectory Simulator & Trend Tracking: Tracks 14-day mission telemetry in local SQLite with sensor-plausibility validation and projects 7-day outcomes across countermeasure protocols (ARED resistance loading, water-wall shelter concept, fluid-loading/thigh cuffs, circadian light scheduling) benchmarked against NASA HRP's 1.0–1.5%/month bone-loss band.

Air-Gapped Local RAG Flight Surgeon Copilot: Uses ChromaDB vector retrieval over curated NASA HRP, NASA OSDR, and CSA Radi-N2 knowledge files with local Ollama LLM inference and a deterministic offline extractive fallback—answering crew questions with exact source citations even in total comms blackouts.

Latency-Aware Ground Handover & Crew Check-In: Queues and exports timestamped Markdown situation reports tailored to ISS, Lunar, or Mars round-trip delay windows, paired with a daily protocol checklist and crew readiness tracker.

Built in Python using Streamlit, Plotly, Pandas, SQLite, ChromaDB, and Ollama (llama3.2 / nomic-embed-text with an offline stdlib embedding fallback), verified by an automated unittest suite
